speaker_role: compiled clip of multiple current school/admissions professionals (appears to be high school counselors and college admissions staff speaking directly to camera)
commercial_incentive: none evident; appears to be an official/informational admissions counseling video
key_insights: An academic recommendation letter should come from a core-subject teacher (history, science, math, social studies, languages); electives like theater or band are considered helpful supplements but not what's required for the academic-teacher letter
Students should ask teachers who know them well, typically from junior and/or senior year, who can cite specific classroom anecdotes about intellectual curiosity or participation
Where possible, get one humanities and one math/science letter, since two letters from similar subject teachers tend to repeat the same observations about writing/class involvement
Students should plan on a calendar about a month ahead of time for when to ask teachers and when the letter needs to be sent

Rather than handing a teacher a resume (which duplicates data already elsewhere in the application), students should discuss specific points they'd like highlighted, since teachers writing multiple letters may otherwise forget or overlook distinguishing details
Admissions readers use recommendations to gauge classroom contribution, resilience, and love of learning, beyond what grades alone convey
specific_numbers_or_facts: Recommenders should be given roughly one month's notice before the letter is due, per one of the speakers
notable_or_distinctive: Structured as a compilation of short statements from several different professionals rather than a single narrator, giving a range of admissions-side and counselor-side perspectives in one short video.
reliability_notes: Very old video (published about 12 years ago); speaker names/titles and institutional affiliations are not stated in the transcript, so specific claims cannot be attributed or verified, and some practices (e.g., specific timelines) may be dated.
